I will keep the full 5.0 mu in my usual wheat-maize rotation because that is the system I know best, it fits Quzhou County well, and with my age and some family labor working off-farm I will not take extra risk by changing crops. I have farmed for 50 years, so I will stay with stable, familiar management: improved winter wheat seed and hybrid summer maize seed, moderate fertilizer instead of pushing for the highest input, and regular well irrigation because I can control water better that way. For wheat, I will put more attention on base fertilizer and a few key irrigations, because wheat here depends on steady moisture through overwintering, jointing, and grain filling. For maize, I will follow the wheat harvest quickly, use hybrid seed for a reliable stand and yield, give enough nitrogen for ear development, and irrigate when summer rain is not enough. I will not make the plan too complicated; I will aim for solid yields with manageable labor, using rotary tillage to keep field work straightforward and pesticide sprays only when needed to protect the crop without overspending.
